Question: What remedy is available with a patient, if a doctor treats a patient on a false diagnosis?
Answer: At the outset, I would like to understand the meaning of the word “ False diagnosis”. For this answer I am taking this word as “ missed diagnosis” or “ wrong diagnosis” and treatment given on the basis of wrong diagnosis. Primarily, as a doctor I accept that the incidence of diagnostic error is high (10–15%,) across the world in the field of medicine.(source: The incidence of diagnostic error in medicine) Why do errors occur? Medicine and health Care is extremely error prone. This is a real major problem and hence the World Health organization has a separate branch called World alliance for patient safety to study this problem. Right from cognitive errors to patient factor… there can be so many reasons. ( source.Diagnostic Errors) Patient safety alliance has created an interesting video to create awareness about this problem and the same can be seen here. If one asks each and every doctor in the world “Have you ever made a mistake in diagnosis?” , One will find that each and every doctor will answer affirmative. “To err is human” is a beautiful report created in the US that details the causes. The root causes of errors go into psychology, education, communication, knowledge deficit ,limitation of medical science to patient behavior and doctor's professional skills and ideology. Every diagnostic error can not be equated to negligence. Actually there is a diagonally different view point of lawyer and patient safety activists on this. If patient feels that there is a negligence the best place to go is consumer court. Trying to initiate criminal machinery is of no use. The Supreme court on many occasions has reiterated that for invoking criminal machinery “Mens rea” which means guity mind or intention is required ( Jacob Mathew Vs State of Punjab) . And no doctor ever has intention to make error. Patient safety alliance ( founded by me) works on increasing awareness about medical errors and propagating “blame free culture”.

Question: Will a gynecologist doctor report to police if a teenager girl is pregnant and above 18?
Answer: A woman above the age of 18 is an adult and she has right and freedom to have consensual sexual intercourse, whether married or unmarried. In other words, a woman below 18 does not have the capacity to give legally valid consent for sexual intercourse as per Indian law ( POSCO Act). Thus pregnancy in a girl below 18 is considered to be out of rape, according to Indian law. A doctor is duty bound to inform the police when the doctors knows that rape has laid to the pregnancy hence doctor needs to inform to the police. Thus, Pregnant woman above 18 , claims that she was a victim of rape and wants health care, doctor had to inform the police. Pregnant woman below 18, even if says that it was consensual, it will be treated as rape in legal terms and hence doctor should inform the police. Lastly, treatment especially when life saving MUST start immediately and police information can wait .

Question: How is the expiry date given to medicines? Suppose a medicine has an expiry date of 31/07/18. Is it safe to consume it now (18/7/18)?

Question: If a pregnant woman will not go to her obstetrician for prenatal care and something is wrong with the baby, that could have been prevented by that care, should the mother be found negligent by a court? Yes or no and why?
Answer: Court canot hold mother guilty for causing death of the fetus in the womb. Let me give a legal and medical reason. Legal reason: The general principles of law ( at least Indian law) are: Fetus in the womb is deemed person. Only when child is born alive , it gains person hood and rights including right of protection accrue. Till then fetus is an appendage of the mother's body and has no right independent of the mother. Medical reason: Lack of nutrition, care, substance abuse, general neglect all can definitely affect the health of the fetus. But none can directly be attributed to death of fetus. The relationship is not so direct. ( No Causa causans ) Most of the above adveresly affect the woman' s health too. So she is also a sufferer. Most of the above have deep rooted causes such as poverty, mal nutrition, lack of education, lack access to health care, male dominant society. In conclusion, not only the fetus but the woman as well is the victim and not perpetrator of neglect. Further pinning her down and putting this burden on her is adding injustice to her.
